variant.stem_override: A 60-year-old man carries an 8-year history of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis (anti-CCP strongly positive, RF 240 IU/mL) and has been managed with subcutaneous methotrexate 20 mg once weekly, hydroxychloroquine, and low-dose prednisone. He now presents with a 6-month history of gradually worsening breathlessness on exertion accompanied by a dry, non-productive cough. On examination, vital signs are: BP 132/78 mmHg, HR 92 beats/min, RR 22 breaths/min, and SpO2 92% breathing room air. Auscultation of the lungs reveals bilateral fine basilar inspiratory crackles ('Velcro rales'). High-resolution chest CT (HRCT protocol) demonstrates bilateral, basilar, peripherally distributed reticular opacities with traction bronchiectasis and honeycombing, consistent with a usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern. Pulmonary function testing shows an FVC of 65% predicted (restrictive pattern) and a DLCO of 50% predicted (markedly reduced). Rheumatoid arthritis disease activity is well controlled, with a DAS28 of 2.5. A chest CT obtained 2 years earlier demonstrated only minimal interstitial abnormalities.
